topic: Suspected cauda equina time to MRI

audits.title: 1249 A Single Centre Analysis of Cauda Equina Referrals Since the ENTICE National Audit
audits.standard: BASS/SBNS national guidelines: MRI before referral for suspected CES
audits.setting: Leeds Neurosurgery department, referrals for suspected cauda equina syndrome

cycle1.result: 15% of referrals had an MRI before referral (15.5% in hours, 14.5% out of hours); 65 had radiologically confirmed CES; 31% increase in referrals compared with before the ENTICE study.

audits.other_findings: 8% of referrals from centres with out-of-hours scanning had no MRI before referral; only 7% of referrals had confirmed CES.
audits.citation: Choudhry H, Vasilla A, Richards O, Schramm M, Kalra N, Sheikh A. 1249 A Single Centre Analysis of Cauda Equina Referrals Since the ENTICE National Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.445.

audits.title: 1060 Audit on Compliance with GIRFT and WM RSN Standards for Management of Cauda Equina Syndrome Patients at UHNM
audits.standard: GIRFT and West Midlands Regional Spinal Network standards for suspected cauda equina syndrome

cycle1.result: Presentation to spinal referral 176 minutes; arrival to MRI 438 minutes; MRI reporting 254 minutes.

cycle2.result: Presentation to spinal referral 60.8 minutes; arrival to MRI 185 minutes; MRI reporting 95.75 minutes.

audits.other_findings: Referral source changed: cycle 1 16 self-presented and 9 GP referrals; cycle 2 22 GP referrals, 2 self-presented, 1 transfer.
audits.citation: Guirguis M, Al-Najjim M, Shahoda W, Jasani V. 1060 Audit on Compliance with GIRFT and WM RSN Standards for Management of Cauda Equina Syndrome Patients at UHNM. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.305.

audits.title: COMPLIANCE WITH THE SUSPECTED CAUDA EQUINA SYNDROME (CES) PATHWAY IN BETSI CADWALADR UNIVERSITY HEALTH BOARD (BCUHB) WEST: A RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT AGAINST NATIONAL STANDARDS
audits.standard: SBNS/BASS guidelines for urgent MRI in suspected cauda equina syndrome
audits.setting: Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board West (Ysbyty Gwynedd)

cycle1.result: 99% scanned in compliance with SBNS/BASS standards; CES found on imaging in 18%.

audits.other_findings: 33% of scans were out of hours and 4% had repeat scans within 6 months; referrals rose from 2.5 to 3.5 per week during the COVID-19 peak.

audits.title: Compliance With the Cauda Equina Pathway: Results of a Closed-Loop Audit.
audits.standard: Local standard operating procedure for acute back pain with suspected cauda equina syndrome, based on BASS/SBNS guidance (senior ED discussion, anal tone and perianal sensation documented, MRI within 24 hours, spinal centre plan documented); no target stated
audits.setting: Non-specialist admitting district hospital (Warrington and Halton Teaching Hospital, per affiliation); emergency department and trauma and orthopaedics, referring to a tertiary spinal centre

cycle1.result: ED assessment and senior discussion 24 (96%); discussion with spinal centre by senior ED doctor 13 (61.9%); anal tone documented 23 (92%); perianal sensation documented 18 (72%); spinal centre plan documented per SOP 5 (20%); MRI within 24 hours 25 (100%).

audits.intervention: Teaching on CES and neurological examination for T&O and ED juniors, posters of the pathway in ED, discussion between T&O and ED on GP referrals, and emails to staff; an electronic SBAR documentation template was also created.

cycle2.result: ED assessment and senior discussion 26 (90%, p=0.727); discussion by senior ED doctor 2 (9%, p=0.000); anal tone documented 28 (97%, p=0.887); perianal sensation documented 28 (97%, p=0.028); spinal centre plan documented 0 (0%, p=0.033); MRI within 24 hours 29 (100%).

audits.other_findings: Referral by a senior ED doctor and documentation of the spinal centre plan worsened, which the authors linked to COVID-19 staffing pressures. Discussion with the spinal centre, post-MRI discussion and management per advice stayed at 100%.
audits.citation: Ago E, Mohammed GDF, Maqsood S, Mohaddis M, Chandran P. Compliance With the Cauda Equina Pathway: Results of a Closed-Loop Audit. Cureus. 2021;13(12):e20843. doi:10.7759/cureus.20843. PMID: 35141091.

audits.title: Suspected Cauda Equina Syndrome: Can the Presence of an Orthopaedic Doctor in the Emergency Department Reduce Waiting Times for MRI Scans and Inpatient Stays?
audits.standard: NICE, BASS and SBNS guidelines and local trust protocol; National Suspected CES Pathway recommends MRI within four hours of request
audits.setting: Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust, a district general hospital with no on-site spinal services; trauma and orthopaedic referrals from the emergency department

cycle1.result: Mean MRI waiting time 12.5 hours (8am-4pm 9.5 h; 4pm-12am 18 h; 12am-8am 8.5 h); same-day discharge 27 (29%); inpatient stay 66 (71%)

audits.intervention: Introduction of a middle-grade trauma and orthopaedic doctor in the emergency department (urgent treatment centre) to assess suspected CES patients

cycle2.result: Mean MRI waiting time 8 hours (8am-4pm 5.5 h; 4pm-12am 13 h; 12am-8am 6.5 h); all MRI scans and reports within 24 hours; same-day discharge 21 (58%); inpatient stay 15 (42%)

audits.other_findings: No patient in cycle 2 had confirmed CES (possible CES in 1, 3%). Admissions fell from an average of 11 to 7 patients per month.
audits.citation: Bakhiet A, Elsayed H, Elamin K, Nath U, Alqubaisi M, Das A, et al.. Suspected Cauda Equina Syndrome: Can the Presence of an Orthopaedic Doctor in the Emergency Department Reduce Waiting Times for MRI Scans and Inpatient Stays?. Cureus. 2023;15(11):e49284. doi:10.7759/cureus.49284. PMID: 38143620.

audits.title: Improving the suspected cauda equina syndrome pathway at a district general hospital: a quality improvement project.
audits.standard: GIRFT National Suspected CES Pathway 2023: emergency MRI within 4 hours of request; local SMART aim of median under 4 hours from ED attendance to MRI within 1 year
audits.setting: Medway Maritime Hospital, Gillingham; district general hospital emergency department without on-site emergency spinal surgery

cycle1.result: Median time from ED presentation to MRI 5.9 hours (IQR 4.9–14.7) although median MRI request to scan was 1.7 hours (IQR 1.1–3.7), meeting the GIRFT target; 8% of patients incorrectly sent to the GP-led MEDOCC service. At PDSA 1: 38% of MRIs unnecessary, 0.5 CES MRIs/day, time to analgesia 5.3 hours (IQR 3.8–7.0), 9% inappropriately triaged to MEDOCC.

audits.intervention: Three PDSA cycles (July 2023 to January 2024): CES working group and trust-level awareness; new locally adapted SOP based on the GIRFT pathway with CES-specific shorter MRI sequences; ED triage and assessment posters, board round, grand round and senior-led teaching. Planned extension of MRI hours was not achieved.

cycle2.period: PDSA 3, cycles run July 2023 to January 2024
cycle2.result: Approximately 27 patients per cycle. Median ED presentation to MRI 5.7 hours (IQR 4.1–14.3), primary aim not met; GIRFT 4-hour request-to-scan target met in all cycles. Unnecessary MRIs fell from 38% to 18%, CES MRIs 0.5/day to 0.4/day, time to analgesia 5.3 to 4.2 hours (IQR 2.7–7.0), and inappropriate MEDOCC referrals 9% to 0%.

audits.other_findings: Time to MRI rose to 9.9 hours in PDSA 2 amid ED pressures and industrial action; 43/81 patients presented at times making same-day MRI unlikely because scanners ran only until 20:00, and by PDSA 3 attendance to MRI request was still a median 3.9 hours.
audits.citation: Conte A, Lingham A, Nagulendran S, Chaudhary U, Alsayeh S, Malkania B, et al.. Improving the suspected cauda equina syndrome pathway at a district general hospital: a quality improvement project. BMJ Open Qual. 2025;14(2):e003081. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2024-003081. PMID: 40441733.
